name: Dusty Orange
lede: Dusty Orange is a warm, slightly muted orange, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Beni'ukon, "red-bronze," literally red dye and turmeric.

sections.title: Red dye and turmeric
sections.body:
Beni'ukon (紅鬱金) is named in the Wikipedia list of Japan's traditional colors for two dye sources together: *beni*, safflower red, and *ukon*, turmeric [1]. Our library also places this color in ISCC-NBS block 53, a block of the 1955 color-naming system that groups it with Maerz and Paul's 1930 names Marygold Yellow, first recorded in 1705, and Damonico, first recorded in 1835 [3].

The nearest named colors on file are [[pastel-orange]] and [[orange]], at 2.6 and 3.3 ΔE [3]. A fifth, slightly farther neighbor is [[cadmium-orange]], 3.8 ΔE away, almost the same [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is the rarest color : our archive finds it in only 18 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.08 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest match is a 1450 icon of Saints Theodore Stratelates and Theodore Tyron, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. With so few matches, no decade or painter stands out reliably, but the color is disproportionately present, relative to their size, in paintings from Norway and India [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
